verdict.summary: Composio has no managed X app, so you must register your own. Before you can create an app, X has to approve a developer account and its binding use-case description, and you will probably need to load prepaid credits. No marketplace review was found. The hard limits are policy ones: going beyond a limited number of end users, or running a service-bureau setup, requires an Enterprise plan. Like and follow endpoints are also no longer available on self-serve tiers.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours (application, billing, app setup, Composio config, privacy policy)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 30-60 minutes if the developer account is approved automatically. Up to about 2 weeks if X reviews it by hand.
verdict.approval_wait: From none (automated for standard use cases, per community reports) to about 2 weeks (an older official figure). Enterprise timing is unknown.

You may need a payment method and loaded credits before any call works (community report)

gates.name: Self-serve (pay-per-use) app used by other X users
gates.unlocks: Other X users can authorize your app. No test-user allowlist or install cap was found in X's docs.

Access tokens expire after 2 hours; refresh tokens are issued only with offline.access

Pay-per-use costs: $0.015 per post, $0.20 per post with a URL, $0.001 per owned read
Community-reported caps: 10,000 posts per 24h per app and 100 posts per 15 min per user
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately after Gate 1. There is no extra review step.

gates.name: Enterprise plan (scaled / multi-customer use)
gates.unlocks: Use beyond a limited number of end users, government end users, and access to the endpoints removed from self-serve tiers. No public marketplace or app-directory listing process was found.

steps.title: Draft the use-case description and privacy policy
steps.detail: Write a specific, accurate use-case description for the developer account and app. X treats it as binding. State what the agent reads and posts, and confirm there is no AI model training, surveillance, profiling or paid engagement. Also draft a privacy policy covering what you collect, how you use and share it, and how people can make requests.
gotchas: A later material change to the use case needs X's prior approval
Community sources say X handles AI and bot use cases differently from standard ones

steps.title: Sign in to the X Developer Console and apply
steps.detail: Go to console.x.com, sign in with the X account that will own the app, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and submit the developer account application with your use-case description.
gotchas: New apps can only be created from the Console, and only with an approved developer account

steps.title: Wait for developer account approval
steps.detail: Community guides say standard use cases are approved automatically. An older X support page says reviews could take up to two weeks, and X may ask for more detail. While the review is pending, the portal shows 'application under review'.

steps.title: Add a payment method and load credits
steps.detail: New signups use pay-per-use pricing. Add a payment card and load credits before making API calls. Saving your first eligible card earns a one-time $20 credit. Your first auto-recharge is matched up to $50. These credits expire after three months.
gotchas: Posts containing a URL cost $0.20 each, compared with $0.015 for a plain post
Check on console.x.com whether Basic or Pro plans are still offered to new developers

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In the Console, create a new app and enter its name, description and use case. The Console then generates the API credentials.
gotchas: You can have at most 3 apps (dev, staging, prod) per service, and you may not register several apps for overlapping use cases

steps.title: Configure User authentication settings
steps.detail: In the app's User authentication settings, turn on OAuth 2.0 and choose a confidential client type (Web App, or Automated App or bot) so X issues a client secret. Paste the Composio callback URL as the callback / redirect URI. X requires an exact match.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The match must be exact, including protocol, path and trailing characters
Native App and Single page App types do not receive a client secret

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with your credentials and trimmed scopes
steps.detail: In Composio, create a twitter auth config using your own OAuth app. Enter the Client ID and Client Secret, and remove scopes your tier cannot use (follows.*, like.*). Keep offline.access so connections get refresh tokens.
gotchas: Without offline.access, tokens stop working after 2 hours
X publishes no OIDC discovery document, so enter the endpoints by hand

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, log in to X, approve the app, and then make a read call and a post call. X validates the client ID only after login, so a wrong client ID shows up as an error after you sign in, not on the authorize page.
gotchas: The authorization code expires after 30 seconds, so the token exchange must happen right away

steps.title: Publish the privacy policy and consent flow
steps.detail: Before other users connect, show your privacy policy before sign-up. Get express, informed consent before the agent acts on anyone's behalf; logging in alone does not count as consent. Show users their X identity after they authenticate, and display Sign in with X at least as prominently as other sign-in options.

steps.title: Decide on Enterprise vs. per-customer apps before scaling
steps.detail: If you will serve more than a limited number of end users, serve government users, or run a multi-customer product, apply for an Enterprise plan or have each customer register their own X app. Shared-app setups risk breaching the service-bureau clause.
gotchas: X can review your use at any time and require a change of access tier

requirements.detail: Required before you can create any app in console.x.com.

Community guides say you must load credits before any calls work under pay-per-use.

requirements.item: Express consent before acting for users
requirements.detail: Authenticating alone is not consent. Opt-in consent is also required to match X users to off-X identifiers.

requirements.item: Enterprise plan for scaled or government use
requirements.detail: Required beyond hobbyist, prototype, early-stage or limited-end-user use, and for government end users.

scopes.effect: Required to get a refresh token. Without it, access tokens expire after 2 hours.

Likes via the API were removed from all self-serve tiers in April 2026. Remove these unless you are on Enterprise.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI does not exactly match the callback URL registered in User authentication settings.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL, including protocol and path, into the app's callback settings.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange fails after the user approves
blockers.cause: The authorization code expires 30 seconds after it is issued.
blockers.fix: Make sure the code is exchanged right away. Composio's hosted flow should handle this; retry the connection.

blockers.symptom: Like or follow actions fail even though the scopes were granted
blockers.cause: X removed following, likes and quote-posts from all self-serve tiers in April 2026.
blockers.fix: Remove these scopes and actions, or get Enterprise access.

blockers.symptom: API calls fail on a new account
blockers.cause: No payment method or credits loaded (community report).
blockers.fix: Add a card and load credits in the Console.

blockers.symptom: App suddenly shows as limited or restricted for policy violations, with no reason given
blockers.cause: X enforcement. Forum reports describe generic notices, sometimes after a paid plan was bought.
blockers.fix: Stay within your stated use case and the restricted-use list, and appeal through the X developer community or support.

blockers.cause: The service-bureau clause, plus community reports that each customer must use their own app.
blockers.fix: Have each customer register their own X app, or get an Enterprise agreement.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for X, so you must create your own X app and enter its Client ID and Secret in a twitter auth config. Register the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config as the X app's callback URL (the toolkit lists https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add as the default). Remove follows.* and like.* from the default scopes, because X removed those endpoints from self-serve tiers. If you serve many customers, X's service-bureau clause may mean each customer needs their own app, or you need an Enterprise plan.

open_questions: There is no current published review time for developer account approval under pay-per-use. The only official figure is the older 'up to two weeks' for Elevated access.
No official user cap or install limit for self-serve apps was found. It is undefined how many end users count as 'limited' before Enterprise is required.
Are Basic and Pro plans still open to new developers, or is every new signup put on pay-per-use? Check on console.x.com.
Should you register Composio's v1 callback (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add) or the URL shown in your auth config? Use the auth config value and confirm it.
Does connecting users through Composio's hosted redirect conflict with X's service-bureau clause? Confirm with X.
Do dm.read, dm.write or users.email trigger extra review? This is undocumented.
The date of the changelog entry that moved app creation to the Console has not been confirmed.
The official pricing and rate-limit pages were not fetched. The per-app and per-user post caps come from community sources.
No marketplace listing, security assessment, or domain or privacy-policy verification step was found for public use.
